title: Aquarium Temperature Drift During Heat Wave
app: WeatherFlow Tempest, Ecowitt, PurpleAir, AirGradient, ESPHome plant sensors, aquarium controllers, and pollen feeds streamed to Splunk HEC via MQTT and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=aquarium:sensor
| stats latest(water_temp_c) as water_temp_c, max(room_temp_c) as room_temp_c by tank
| where room_temp_c>28 AND (water_temp_c<23 OR water_temp_c>27)
| sort - room_temp_c
description: Uses Aquarium climate telemetry telemetry to monitor tank temperature control during hot weather in index=personal.
value: Splunk turns the feed into an operational check for heat-wave days that stress fish or cooling gear, so the signal does not stay buried inside separate consumer apps or exports.
implementation: Ingest Aquarium climate telemetry data through its real API, export, MQTT bridge, or open-source connector into `index=personal`; preserve the fields referenced in the SPL and schedule the search on a daily cadence.
visualization: Tank table of water and room temperature.
grandmaExplanation: It notices tank temperature control during hot weather so you can spot heat-wave days that stress fish or cooling gear before it becomes annoying.
